content.text: Section 24 fully matches our preferred position, and no hidden change-of-control trigger exists elsewhere (§ 9 termination triggers are limited to breach/insolvency, and § 9.2 expressly excludes benign reorganizations).

input.quote: 24.1 Customer may assign this Agreement or an Order Form without Vendor's consent to an Affiliate or to a successor in a merger, reorganization, acquisition, or sale of all or substantially all assets or business to which the Agreement relates.
input.rationale: Section 24 already reaches our preferred position on every element. Section 24.1 gives Customer an unrestricted right to assign to an Affiliate or an M&A successor without Vendor consent (notice only). Section 24.2 binds Vendor asymmetrically in our favour: no assignment, delegation of material performance, or transfer by change of control without our prior written consent (reasonableness qualified only as to capable, financially sound assignees), plus an absolute bar on assignment to a direct Customer competitor without our consent. Section 24.3 applies a mutual not-unreasonably-withheld standard to residual assignments and voids non-conforming attempts. Section 24.4 expressly denies Vendor any right to terminate, suspend, reprice, accelerate Fees, or reduce service on Customer's change of control and requires cooperation with successor administrative changes. Searches for "change of control" and "assign" surface no other trigger; § 9 termination rights are limited to material breach and insolvency, and § 9.2 confirms a lawful reorganization is not itself grounds for termination. Section 13 also lets Customer transfer licence rights to an Affiliate or successor in connection with a Section 24 assignment, and § 30.5 preserves enforcement rights for permitted successors. No redline needed.
